title: Call provenance & reproducibility metadata scratch
body:
Context / why this exists:
- We need a minimal, consistent way to attach provenance and replay metadata to every inference call that matters for debugging, audits, and reruns.
- Hosted + dedicated + private deployments all need tooling to: a) trace what model & config produced output b) replay with bit-for-bit determinism where possible or closest approximation otherwise c) surface operator-friendly diffs.

Goals / non-goals:
- Goals: compact metadata envelope, stable API shape across environments, privacy-safe (PII excluded by default), enable deterministic replay when model checkpoint + runtime config + tokenization are identical.
- Non-goals: perfection for nondeterministic models (we accept approximations), replacing full observability pipeline (this complements tracing).

High-level design (sketch):
- Attach a top-level provenance envelope to request and to stored response. Envelope fields (minimal first, expanded later):
  - request_id: string (uuid v4)  -- primary correlation id
  - timestamp: ISO-8601
  - model_id: string (catalog id + pinned-version) e.g. "redwood/gptx:2026-02-04"
  - model_fingerprint: string (short hash of model binary manifest, not weights) e.g. sha256:abcd1234 (helps map identical artifacts across registries)
  - runtime_config_id: string (pointer to hashed runtime config blob)
  - tokenizer_fingerprint: string (tokenizer version/hash)
  - decode_settings: string list / compact map (temp, top_k, top_p, beam_size) serialized as stable key order e.g. "temp=0.2;top_p=0.95"
  - seed_hint: optional int/string (if client supplies seed to make sampling deterministic)
  - client_sdk: optional string (sdk+version)
  - invocation_path: list of short tags (e.g., ["api","chat","function-call"]) serialized as CSV or pipe 
  - provenance_level: enum [minimal,audit,verbose]  -- controls how much runtime trace to capture

- For responses we add:
  - response_id: string (separate)
  - matched_cache_key: optional string (if cached)
  - kv_prefix_snapshot_ref: optional string (for prompt-prefix caching snapshots)
  - deterministic_replay_key: optional string (hash over request + model_fingerprint + runtime_config_id + tokenizer_fingerprint + seed_hint + decode_settings)
  - recorded_sampling_stream_ref: optional (only for provenance_level=verbose) -> internal blaze storage ref (not exposed to clients by default)

API shape examples (HTTP JSON):
- Client request header (simple):
  X-Redwood-Provenance: {request_id, client_sdk}
  (we keep header tiny; full envelope in body can be requested with ?include_provenance=1)

- Body envelope (when requested):
  {
    "provenance": "request_id=..., timestamp=..., model_id=..., model_fp=..., runtime_cfg=...",
    "input": "...",
    "options": {...}
  }
(We canonicalize provenance into a single string field for compact logs and to avoid schema churn; server can expand into structured metadata in internal stores.)

Storage / tracing:
- Lightweight path: store compact envelope with response record in usual DB (dynamodb/postgres), deterministic_replay_key stored as indexed column.
- Heavyweight path (audit / verbose): store additional artifacts (sampling streams, token-level decisions, kv-snapshots) in long-term blob store with TTL and access controls.
- For private deployments: blob store may be customer-managed; runtime_config_id must map to local config store.

Deterministic replay semantics (best-effort):
- Replay is considered deterministic if: model_fingerprint, tokenizer_fingerprint, runtime_config_id, decode_settings, seed_hint match and runtime reports no non-deterministic kernels used.
- If deterministic_replay_key matches existing replay artifacts we provide a replay token that triggers a special "replay mode" in runtime (strict seeds, fixed rng).
- We accept that some models are inherently nondeterministic (float nondeterminism across GPU families). In those cases we produce a "replay_similarity_score" approximated by comparing token probabilities across a short prefix.

Privacy & compliance notes:
- By default we do NOT store raw client-provided PII in provenance blobs. Instead store references/hashed forms.
- Provide a per-tenant toggle to opt-in to richer captures for support cases (audit/legal).

Implementation concerns / tradeoffs:
- Compact single-string provenance vs fully structured JSON: single-string is log-friendly and easier for downstream indexing, but less ergonomic when debugging. Proposal: store compact string in response record + structured JSON in internal blob for verbose captures.
- Backwards compatibility: new fields should be optional; use runtime_config_id to map older configs.
- Performance: adding provenance must not add >2% p99 latency. Keep capture async for verbose artifacts.

Operational UX / Console support:
- Console should show the provenance envelope inline on a response view, with quick actions: copy deterministic_replay_key, open sampling artifact (if present), replay request.
- For dedicated/private: provide an admin page to map runtime_config_id -> human readable config and to assert replay preconditions.

Questions / open items (TODOs):
- 1) Exact canonical format for deterministic_replay_key (order/serialization). RFC: lexicographic key order, stable separators, then sha256 hex.
- 2) How to represent model_fingerprint for ensembles / cascades? (list or composite hash?)
- 3) What is the minimal set of decode settings necessary for reproducing outputs? (should we capture logits processor chain?)
- 4) Should we allow client-specified provenance fields (e.g., external correlation id) and how to authenticate them?
- 5) UI/Console: redaction controls for stored artifacts per-tenant.

Next steps (practical):
- Draft API header + body examples for SDKs (python/node), add to SDK quickstarts. (owner: Marco)
- Implement deterministic_replay_key generator util in runtime (owner: Evelyn)
- Hook minimal envelope into hosted path; keep verbose capture behind feature flag.

Notes to self: keep this small and iterative. Prototype with only: request_id, model_id, model_fp, runtime_config_id, tokenizer_fp, decode_settings, deterministic_replay_key. Add verbose streaming capture after proof-of-value.

Ascii sketch (how console might present):

[Response view]
> output: "..."
provenance: request_id=.. | model=redwood/gptx:2026-02-04 | model_fp=sha256:abcd | cfg=cfg-0f12 | key=deadbeef...
-> [Replay] [Open sampling stream] [Map cfg]

End of scratch.
